title: B2B supplier differentiation → Floras embed
floras_mechanism: For B2B suppliers selling into enterprise buyers — packaging, ingredients, contract manufacturing, industrial inputs — Floras embeds a small climate contribution into invoices or product lines. The supplier differentiates versus competitors: enterprise customers receive Floras-linked value tied to purchases, which can support the buyer's Scope 3 narratives. This is a supplier win-account story, not buyer wallet accumulation at the brand level.
pain_signals: supplier competes primarily on price and spec sheets
enterprise customers demand sustainability proof from vendors
key account renewals require stronger ESG differentiation
buyer RFPs include supplier sustainability criteria
difficulty standing out beyond recycled content or material claims
sales team needs a concrete climate value prop for enterprise accounts
budget_source: Key account budget; sales enablement budget; sustainability commercial budget; contract margin allocation
safe_claims: Floras can help suppliers differentiate enterprise offerings with transaction-linked climate value
Enterprise customers can receive Floras tied to qualifying purchases from the supplier
Supplier-embedded Floras can support buyer Scope 3 engagement without the supplier claiming full emissions reductions
Certificates and project allocation can support enterprise customer reporting when consistent with research
conditional_claims: If the supplier serves CPG or retail brands, Floras can align with those buyers' supplier sustainability programs
If contract volume is high, Floras embed can scale with transaction activity
If the supplier already reports sustainability metrics, Floras can complement with transaction-linked funding evidence
avoid_claims: The supplier's product becomes carbon-neutral by default
Floras replaces material reduction, recycled content, or lifecycle assessment
Every enterprise customer automatically achieves Scope 3 reductions
Floras is the same as the brand buyer accumulating wallet value at Pepsi scale — this is supplier-side embed

output_templates.one_liner: Help {company_name}'s enterprise customers see climate-linked value on every qualifying purchase.
output_templates.short_pitch: {company_name} competes for enterprise accounts where sustainability is increasingly part of the RFP. Floras lets you embed a small climate contribution into qualifying transactions so your customers receive transaction-linked climate value — not a generic offset story. That gives your sales team a differentiated, enterprise-ready narrative: purchases from {company_name} can connect to verified project allocation and certificates that support customer Scope 3 and supplier engagement reporting.

objections_and_responses.objection: Our customers only care about price and lead times.
objections_and_responses.response: Floras targets accounts where sustainability is already in RFPs and renewals. It gives commercial teams a differentiator when spec and price are table stakes — especially for strategic enterprise accounts evaluating supplier ESG performance.

objections_and_responses.objection: We are not the brand — we cannot speak to their Scope 3 wallet.
objections_and_responses.response: Correct — this case is supplier-side embed. The pitch is how Floras helps your customers receive climate-linked value through your transactions, strengthening your account story without pretending to be the brand's enterprise wallet program.

objections_and_responses.objection: Sustainability is handled by our customer's sustainability team, not procurement.
objections_and_responses.response: Floras connects to procurement activity — the surface area your sales team already owns. It gives buyers' procurement and sustainability teams a shared transaction-linked mechanism rather than a disconnected annual offset purchase.
